card.name: Plain words in patient-advice sentences
card.fires_on: Common everyday words (body parts, 'doctor', 'down', 'not') in the middle of simple advice or symptom sentences, just before a list or a continuing phrase. No single word type dominates.

modes.label: Body parts and people
modes.description: A body part or 'doctor' ends a phrase such as 'Tell your doctor' or 'in the arms and legs'.
modes.example: Tell your<< doctor>> if you or your child has any heart

modes.label: Short action words
modes.description: A small word like 'down' or 'not' follows a verb in an instruction or warning.
modes.example: You can lessen your risk of side effects like fainting by sitting<< down>> for 15 minutes after each shot

modes.label: Household objects
modes.description: A plain noun such as clothing or roof sits in a how-to or cause list.
modes.example: Once installed on your<< roof>> the system immediately begins generating electricity, which
